prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1416; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a rear-end collision at a low-speed intersection and said she felt neck and upper back discomfort within the hour. She is not represented by counsel and confirmed she is willing to speak with me directly.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy file and confirmed the driver is named on the policy and the coverage was in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the underwriting file suggests the vehicle damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 3: Photos submitted by the claimant show damage to the rear bumper and trunk that is consistent with the impact described. A few old scratches are visible on the lower panel, which may be older than this crash and will be noted for the appraiser.

Entry 4: Police report and two drivers' statements place the claimant in the vehicle at the time of the collision. No independent witnesses were located, so the account rests on the parties' statements and the physical evidence.

Entry 5: Spoke with the claimant again and she gave the same account of how the collision happened, including speed, direction, and sequence of events. Her description has not changed across each conversation so far.

Entry 6: Medical records show a back strain, which matches the kind and force of a rear impact of this type. No prior injury to the same body area is known from her records or from questions asked during intake.

Entry 7: Treatment followed a usual course of physical therapy and tapered off as her symptoms improved, with discharge notes recording steady progress. Reserves will be reviewed against the current treatment status and final medical bills.
